scenario.name: AWS CIRT & CISA Cloud DFIR — AWS IAM PassRole + Lambda Privilege Escalation & StopLogging Tampering
scenario.overview: Imagine a cloud forensics case study of a shadow-administrator takeover: an ordinary developer who cannot grant themselves master keys uses a delegated robot builder to pass a powerful role to a custom script, commands that script to attach full Administrator ribbons onto their own badge, and then tries to unplug the central security recorder, leaving three unmistakable sequential entries in the tamper-proof cloud ledger. In this scenario (T1098.001, AWS CIRT & CISA Cloud DFIR, AWS IAM PassRole + Lambda Privilege Escalation & StopLogging Tampering), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: iAM Privilege Escalation via iam:PassRole +, then lambda Invocation, then cloudTrail Anti-Forensics Attempt Blocked. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering IAM Privilege Escalation via iam:PassRole +, then Lambda Invocation, then CloudTrail Anti-Forensics Attempt Blocked, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on SIEM Event 201 correlated across the documented kill chain.

specs.value: Restrict iam:PassRole with explicit Resource ARNs (never Resource: "*") and apply IAM Permissions Boundaries to all developer and CI/CD roles.

stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation (T1098.001 - Account Manipulation: IAM PassRole Escalation)

stages.title: Stage 2: Lambda Invocation & Shadow Admin Policy Attachment (iam:AttachUserPolicy)
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1098.001 - AttachUserPolicy AdministratorAccess)
stages.description: Triggering the newly built helper function immediately, the developer watches the function step into the IAM control room under its privileged role and attach the full Administrator policy straight back onto the developer own identity. When dev-ci-user invokes the function, the Lambda execution environment assumes AdminLambdaExecutionRole and calls iam:AttachUserPolicy to attach arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AdministratorAccess directly to dev-ci-user (logged in Network Event 200 with CloudTrailEvent=iam.amazonaws.com : AttachUserPolicy, ExecutingPrincipal=AssumedRole/AdminLambdaExecutionRole/metrics-sync-helper, ElevatedTargetUser=dev-ci-user, AttachedPolicyArn=arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AdministratorAccess so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Next, the follow-up artifact userIdentity.arn: "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/AdminLambdaExecutionRole/metrics-sync-helper" runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , userIdentity.arn: "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/AdminLambdaExecutionRole/metrics-s so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1098.001 during "Lambda Invocation & Shadow Admin Policy Attachment , iam:AttachUserPolicy" , When dev-ci-user invokes the function, the Lambda execution environment assumes AdminLambdaExecutionRole and calls iam:AttachUserPolicy to attach arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AdministratorAccess directly to dev-ci-user while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). keySpecs.value: Alert immediately via Amazon EventBridge / SIEM on any iam:AttachUserPolicy, iam:PutUserPolicy, or iam:CreateAccessKey call originating from a Lambda function or non-Terraform role.

stages.title: Stage 3: CloudTrail Anti-Forensics Attempt (cloudtrail:StopLogging / DeleteTrail) Blocked by SCP
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1562.008 - Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Cloud Logs)
stages.description: Moments after receiving full Administrator keys, the intruder attempts to turn off or erase the central cloud activity trail, ironically stamping the loudest possible red flare right onto the final recorded page. Now holding AdministratorAccess, the actor calls cloudtrail:StopLogging on the organization trail to blind subsequent actions. AWS Organizations Service Control Policies (SCPs) deny the call with errorCode="AccessDenied" while CloudTrail records the StopLogging attempt for DFIR investigators (logged in Network Event 403 with CloudTrailEvent=cloudtrail.amazonaws.com : StopLogging, TargetedTrail=org-audit-trail, ErrorCode=AccessDenied , Blocked by Organization SCP, MitreTechnique=T1562.008 , Disable Cloud Logs so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes CloudTrail Event: eventSource="cloudtrail.amazonaws.com" eventName="StopLogging" (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , CloudTrail Event: eventSource="cloudtrail.amazonaws.com" eventName="StopLogging" via System so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1562.008 during "CloudTrail Anti-Forensics Attempt , cloudtrail:StopLogging / DeleteTrail Blocked by SCP" , Now holding AdministratorAccess, the actor calls cloudtrail:StopLogging on the organization trail to blind subsequent actions while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact errorCode: "AccessDenied" (Blocked by AWS Organizations SCP Deny cloudtrail:StopLogging) runs (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , errorCode: "AccessDenied" , Blocked by AWS Organizations SCP Deny cloudtrail:StopLogging agai so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1562.008 during "CloudTrail Anti-Forensics Attempt , cloudtrail:StopLogging / DeleteTrail Blocked by SCP" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ CloudTrail cloudtrail:StopLogging attempt by dev-ci-user / ⇠#3 RESP 403) from Node ③ (#3 AWS IAM & Lambda API) to Node ④ (#4 Lambda (AdminExecRole)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 AttachUserPolicy (AdminAccess)).
